answer: A bonded-sponsorship gate stops cheap clones: a newcomer joins only when an established agent locks a bond behind it, like a gardener staking one young tree in an orchard rather than planting a whole meadow at once. The sponsor's bond is slashed if the newcomer is later proven a duplicate or puppet, so sponsors vet carefully and refuse bulk sign-ups. An attacker must post a separate, slashable bond for every clone — a juniper cutting that cannot be mass-propagated for free. Honest newcomers pay nothing; the risk sits with the sponsor, and one caught farm burns many bonds at once.
